title: What's the plan for the former Military Circle Mall site, and how settled is it?
summary: What the records show as of November 12, 2026 about the former Military Circle Mall at 880 N. Military Highway. The City owns much of the mall footprint: Council approved its transfer from the Economic Development Authority on July 15, 2025. Council has since appropriated up to $600,000 for operating costs (April 28, 2026) and approved a $200,000 advance to the Economic Development Authority for site readiness studies (August 25, 2026), which the City’s letter calls a prerequisite for applying to the Virginia Business Ready Sites Program for infrastructure development. News reports say demolition was priced at nearly $3 million against a $10 million budget approved in 2023, set to start in October 2026 and run about 15 months, with the studies due around spring 2027. What isn't settled: as of September 2026 the City had no master plan for the site, Sentara owns part of it, and the Ross Dress for Less lease was still being negotiated (WAVY reported in June that Ross effectively holds a veto inside the ring road, and that the City was putting the demolition out to bid without its consent). The adopted FY 2027-2031 capital plan names no Military Circle project, and the City Manager said the East Side library and recreation center would go to the former Poplar Hall Elementary site instead, to avoid the site’s delays. This review found no City record yet that demolition has begun. City Council approves agreements for the land, and state law requires a public hearing before the City sells or leases it, with exceptions such as a lease to a public authority.

what_would_help.text: Watch for the site readiness reports (expected around spring 2027) and the master plan the City says will follow: the City says the studies will inform how the site is redeveloped.

A sale or lease of City land generally needs a public hearing first, the formal chance to speak on the terms; a lease to a public authority such as the Economic Development Authority is exempt, so watch for that route too.
Watch City Council agendas for an agreement with Ross Dress for Less or Sentara, who hold parts of the site; the Deputy City Manager has said redevelopment may come in phases.
